issues.description: validate_conda complects existence, permission, and identity checks with side-effecting subprocess execution
issues.detail: The function intertwines four distinct concerns: path-is-string, file-exists, file-is-executable, and 'running this binary with --version identifies as a conda-family tool'. The last is a side-effecting probe against the user-supplied path during a preference page validation callback. These should be decomposed: a pure predicate over a value (path string), separated from the act of executing an arbitrary user-chosen binary. As written, selecting a file in the preferences dialog runs that file as a subprocess. That is identity-and-time entangled with value-validation, and it has security implications the simple alternative would not.

issues.description: Tool detection by substring match on stdout is incidental complexity masquerading as identification
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"])` is the kind of 'easy' check that is not simple. 'mamba' is a substring of 'micromamba', so the iteration is redundant; more importantly, the identity of the tool is being inferred from a free-form version string rather than from a value the system already knows. The decomposed version is: parse the version output into a value (name, version), then ask predicates of that value. The current shape will quietly accept any binary whose --version output contains the literal 'conda' anywhere.

`if conda_executable == "": return True` treats the absence of a value as a successful validation. Absence and validity are different facts about the world. The caller (the preferences page) should decide what 'empty' means in its own context; the validator should answer one question about one value. As written, the validator returns True for a path that, by every other criterion in the function, is not a conda executable.

issues.description: Two config keys (`custom_conda` + `conda_path`) encode one fact, and the kernelspec code has to reconstruct it
issues.detail: The state is split: a boolean toggle and a path string, with the rule 'use the path only if the toggle is true' enforced at every read site. kernelspec.py now contains a nested conditional that re-derives the intended value from those two keys. The simpler model is a single value: either the configured path (a string) or nothing. The toggle is a UI affordance, not a fact about the world; storing both invites the inevitable drift where `custom_conda=True` but `conda_path=''`, or `custom_conda=False` but a stale path lingers. Decompose: one source of truth for 'the user-specified conda executable, if any', plus a separate UI state if needed.

issues.description: `filters='*.exe'` on a cross-platform file picker is place-oriented thinking
issues.detail: The browse dialog filters to `*.exe`, but conda/mamba/micromamba on macOS and Linux are not `.exe` files. This is a small instance of the larger pattern: a UI assumption (Windows file extension) leaking into a value (path to a binary). On non-Windows platforms the user will see an empty file list by default. The filter should depend on the platform, or be 'all files', and the validation should be the gate.

issues.description: `run_program(...).communicate()` without timeout or explicit lifecycle is incidental complexity at the edge
issues.detail: Executing the user-supplied path with no timeout means a misbehaving binary (or a path the user accidentally pointed at a long-running program) can hang the preferences UI. The function catches all exceptions and returns False, so the failure mode is silent. A simple version: bounded subprocess call with explicit timeout, returning a value (success, stdout, stderr) that the predicate can inspect.

issues.description: `edit.setFocus()` added to `select_file` couples file selection with focus management for all callers
issues.detail: The change to `widgets/config.py` is small but it alters the behavior of every existing call site of `select_file` across the codebase, not just the new conda field. That is a shared mutable behavior change made to serve one new caller. If only the new field needs focus after selection, the caller should request it; if it is a general improvement, that is a separable change with its own justification.

review.summary: The feature is useful and the diff is small, but it carries the characteristic shape of "easy" code that is not yet "simple." The core values — "the conda executable the user wants to use" — are split across two config keys with a derivation rule re-implemented at the call site, and the validator complects path-existence, executability, and a side-effecting subprocess probe with substring-matching on free-form output. The right decomposition is one value (an optional path), one pure predicate over that value, and a single bounded act of running the binary to identify it — separated, not intertwined. The cross-platform `*.exe` filter and the unrelated `setFocus()` change are smaller instances of the same pattern: UI defaults leaking into values, and one caller's needs changing shared behavior. The question that should have been asked first: what single fact about the world does this preference represent, and where does it live?
